prompt: Why did agenda move from SQLite to PostgreSQL in this lesson?
hint: What does the last section of the lesson rely on?

choices.text: SQLite cannot store dates with a time zone
choices.why: Django stores them in UTC either way.

choices.text: SQLite has no row locks
choices.why: Right: concurrent registrations need them, and select_for_update does nothing there.

choices.text: Django 6.1 dropped support for SQLite
choices.why: It still supports it; agenda used it in lessons 2 and 3.

choices.text: SQLite has no foreign keys
choices.why: It has them.

prompt: agenda's DATABASES names no user, password or host. How does Django get in?

choices.text: PostgreSQL accepts anyone on localhost without checking
choices.why: It checks; the check is the operating-system user.

choices.text: psycopg reads the password from ~/.pgpass by default
choices.why: There is no password involved here.

choices.text: The superuser role skips authentication
choices.why: Superuser is about permissions once connected.

choices.text: By peer authentication over the socket
choices.why: Right: as the role ana, whose name matches the login.

choices.why: createdb ran as ana and the name was agenda.

choices.text: The server is stopped
choices.why: A stopped server gives a socket error, not this one.

prompt: A settings file names USER 'agenda' with no HOST, and PostgreSQL answers Peer authentication failed. Which change follows the lesson's advice?

choices.text: Rename your Linux account to agenda
choices.why: That fixes it by accident and breaks everything else.

choices.text: Make the agenda role a superuser
choices.why: Peer authentication fails before permissions matter.

choices.text: Connect over TCP with HOST 'localhost' and the role's password
choices.why: Right. Lesson 15 does exactly that.

choices.text: Restart PostgreSQL
choices.why: Nothing about the server's state is wrong.

prompt: What does related_name="registrations" on Registration.event give you?

choices.why: No column is added to events.

choices.text: event.registrations
choices.why: Right: the way back from an event, a manager for its registrations.

choices.text: A name for the foreign key constraint
choices.why: The constraint gets a generated name.

choices.text: A second table joining events to registrations
choices.why: That would be many-to-many; this is a foreign key.

prompt: Which of these came from the models into the SQL that sqlmigrate printed? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: CHECK ("capacity" >= 0)
choices.why: Right, from PositiveIntegerField.

choices.text: CONSTRAINT "one_registration_per_email" UNIQUE ("event_id", "email")
choices.why: Right, from Meta.constraints.

choices.text: ON DELETE CASCADE on the foreign key
choices.why: Django applies CASCADE itself; the SQL foreign key had DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED.

choices.text: An index on events_registration.event_id
choices.why: Right. Django indexes every foreign key.

choices.text: A DEFAULT for created_at
choices.why: auto_now_add is filled in Python.

choices.text: No: the seed stored the wrong time

choices.text: No: USE_TZ should be False
choices.why: USE_TZ is what keeps this right.

choices.text: Yes: 19:00 at UTC-3 is 22:00 UTC

choices.text: Only by chance, since November has no daylight saving there

prompt: How many rows did seed.py create in events_event?
Why did the 0002 migration add the column with DEFAULT '' and then drop the default?
hint: Existing rows, and where Django keeps defaults.

choices.text: Old rows need a value; defaults live in Python
choices.why: Right. The three events got '', then the default went, since Django keeps defaults in Python.

choices.text: PostgreSQL forbids text columns without a default
choices.why: It allows them.

choices.text: blank=True requires a database default
choices.why: blank is about forms, not the database.

choices.text: To make the migration reversible

prompt: A migration that already ran on your colleague's machine has a mistake. What does the lesson say to do?
hint: What happens to an edited migration on a database that already ran it?

choices.text: Edit it and ask everyone to run migrate
choices.why: migrate skips it there: it is already recorded as applied.

choices.text: Write a new migration that fixes it
choices.why: Right. History is only added to.

choices.text: Delete the migrations folder and run makemigrations
choices.why: That orphans every database that already ran them.

choices.text: Run migrate --fake on both machines
choices.why: Faking hides the difference instead of fixing it.

prompt: print(events.query) showed LIKE Community% without quotes. What does that tell you?

choices.text: Django forgot to escape the parameter, which is an injection risk
choices.why: The query that ran had the parameter passed separately.

prompt: Why is connection.queries a development tool and not something to read in production?

choices.text: It slows queries down tenfold
choices.why: Cost is not the reason given.

choices.text: It shows passwords
choices.why: It shows SQL and parameters.

choices.text: Django keeps it only while DEBUG is on
choices.why: Right, and DEBUG is never on in production.

choices.text: Only superusers can read it
choices.why: Any code can.

prompt: explain() printed Seq Scan on events_event. On a table of a million events, what would that line suggest?
hint: What does a sequential scan read?

choices.text: Nothing: Seq Scan is always the fastest plan
choices.why: For three rows it is; for a million it reads them all.

choices.text: A full-table read; an index would help
choices.why: Right: the venue filter reads every row. Reading plans in depth is sql-databases' job.

choices.text: That the ORM wrote bad SQL and raw SQL is needed
choices.why: The SQL is fine; the table lacks an index.

choices.text: That ordering must be removed
choices.why: Sorting is a separate node in the plan.

prompt: Who refused the second registration for bruno@example.org on Django Night in the shell?

choices.text: The RegistrationForm's email validator
choices.why: The shell used no form.

choices.text: register() in services.py
choices.why: The shell called objects.create directly.

choices.text: PostgreSQL, through the unique constraint
choices.why: Right: IntegrityError, duplicate key value violates unique constraint.

choices.text: CsrfViewMiddleware
choices.why: No request was involved.

prompt: Without select_for_update, how many registrations did crowd.py leave for the 12-seat workshop?
Why does select_for_update only work inside transaction.atomic()?
hint: How long does a lock last?

choices.text: atomic() is what sends FOR UPDATE to the database
choices.why: The QuerySet sends it; atomic() bounds it.

choices.text: Outside a transaction PostgreSQL ignores the lock silently
choices.why: Django refuses it before it reaches PostgreSQL.

choices.text: A lock lasts as long as its transaction
choices.why: Right. Without one, it would end with the statement.

choices.text: Threads share one connection otherwise
choices.why: Each thread has its own connection either way.

prompt: The annotated list came back as Async, Testing, Django, though Meta.ordering says starts_at. Why?
hint: What kind of query was it?

choices.text: Count sorts by the number of registrations
choices.why: Async has 12, but the order is not by count.

choices.text: The registrations were inserted in that order, and rows come back that way
choices.why: Insertion order is not a promise SQL makes.

choices.text: Aggregating queries skip the model's default order
choices.why: Right: Django leaves Meta.ordering out of a GROUP BY since 3.1. Say order_by() when order matters.

choices.text: PostgreSQL sorts aggregated rows by id
choices.why: No sort was asked for, so the order is whatever the plan gives.

prompt: A teammate proposes counting the free seats in the template, with {{ event.capacity|add:... }}, to avoid the lock. What does that miss?
hint: Where is the decision made, and when?

choices.text: Templates cannot do arithmetic
choices.why: add does arithmetic; that is not the problem.

choices.text: The count must be checked at the insert
choices.why: Right: the page is drawn before the POST, and only the lock makes the count true when it is used.

choices.text: The template would need select_related
choices.why: Related loading does not make a count current.

choices.text: Nothing; showing free seats replaces the check
choices.why: Two people can see one free seat at once.
